fixtures.trader_label: A key-level rejection entry can be two momentum candles, doji then momentum, pinbar then momentum, inside bar then momentum, or shrinking candles heading into the key level, rejection, then a reverse momentum candle. Rejection by itself is not enough.
Every strong move is not displacement. There are strong bullish and bearish momentum candles that are not displacement.

One of only two pre-break exceptions: genuine displacement drives toward the key level; the trader watches the THIRD candle of that displacement drive and enters early only if that third candle is still a directional momentum candle near the key level. If the third candle reverses control, no entry. FVG formation is irrelevant to this entry rule and is not required.

The other pre-break exception: after the level has already been tested, price can return and attack/test it again with breakout momentum; that momentum attack can authorize entry before a completed candle has printed beyond the key level.

When price first prints beyond a key level, that first print is not the entry by itself; a following momentum candle can confirm. If the initial break is weak, price may pull back and the trader checks the 15-minute chart for a three-bar continuation entry.
The liquidity cluster appeared before the FVG, price reacted there and did not need to trade into the farther FVG. Whichever meaningful reaction area appears first owns TP.
On ranging days, do not mark fresh key zones too close to the range. Draw/authorize key zones where price has room to break out and travel before it reaches the key-level zone.
